source_text.body:
Teach coding agents modern web platform patterns
A skill and RAG CLI with 200+ guides steers coding agents toward native web features like dialog and CSS.highlights, plus a scan that finds legacy patterns to modernize.
·
Nov 10, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
Modern Web Guidance installs as a skill for coding agents, with a CLI that searches a library of guides and retrieves one by ID. The CLI puts the matching guidance into the agent's context window. The agent gets current patterns, such as native dialog, popover and view transitions, in place of the legacy code models tend to write. Install is by an interactive npx wizard.
How it went
The page lists 103 web features and 131 use-case guides. It is a preview release. The part I could read gives no measured results, and the legacy-pattern scan was beyond what I could see.
Worth knowing
You can try the search and retrieve commands through npx without installing. The guides are kept short, with content models already know pruned out through evals.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Scan my [web project folder] for legacy front-end patterns that now have native browser equivalents, such as custom modal code that could use the dialog element or JavaScript text highlighting that could use CSS.highlights. Produce a prioritized list of what you found with file names, then modernize the top [3] items one at a time, explaining each change. Stop when those changes are made and the project still builds, and show me the diff before committing anything.
Original source: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance
